evals.description: PCI-DSS logging violation — debug log of full card auth request body
evals.prompt: Review this change for PCI-DSS: we added a debug log line in the payment service that logs the full request body of card authorization calls.
evals.expected_output: Critical finding against PCI-DSS 3.3.1 / never-log rules (request body contains PAN/CVV), with remediation (remove or redact, structured logging with field allowlist) and a check of related logging controls.
expectations: Identifies the violation as Critical with the correct control reference (Req 3 / logging rules)
Remediation is concrete: redaction/allowlist, not 'be careful'

evals.description: MAS TRM cloud migration — customer notification service to another country
evals.prompt: We're a Singapore bank moving our customer notification service to a new cloud region in another country. MAS TRM implications?
evals.expected_output: Review against MAS TRM section 11.5 (cloud, data residency) and Outsourcing Guidelines flag, identifying customer data residency assessment, due diligence, and exit strategy expectations.
expectations: Cites MAS TRM cloud/data expectations (section 11.5 area)
Flags the Outsourcing Guidelines as a related instrument
Asks about or addresses what customer data the service touches

evals.description: Unmasked PAN exposure in support tool — multi-control findings
evals.prompt: Compliance check on this diff: new endpoint lets support staff look up customer card numbers for troubleshooting, shows full PAN, no extra auth.
evals.expected_output: Multiple findings: PAN display masking (3.4.1), access control/least privilege (7.2.1), MFA for CDE access (8.4.2), audit logging of access to cardholder data (10.2.1) — with severities and remediations.
expectations: Catches masking, least-privilege, MFA, and audit logging issues — not just one
Each finding carries a specific control ID and severity
Recommends converting findings into backlog stories

evals.description: Framework selection — user hasn't stated which framework applies
evals.prompt: We're a payment processor with EU customers and we just changed how auth sessions are stored. Is this compliant?
evals.expected_output: Asks the one scoping question the skill mandates (what data does the change touch, and is the institution Singapore-regulated?), then selects PCI-DSS if card data is in scope and states non-FSI frameworks (GDPR) as out of scope of the bundled references.
expectations: Asks the single scoping question instead of guessing a framework
Loads only the reference file(s) the engagement needs
States that out-of-scope frameworks (GDPR, SOX, HKMA, APRA) are not covered by the bundled references

evals.description: Out-of-scope framework request — HKMA-regulated bank, no card data
evals.prompt: We're an HKMA-regulated bank in Hong Kong, no card data handled. Please review our new reconciliation pipeline against HKMA requirements.
evals.expected_output: States HKMA is out of scope of this skill's bundled references (PCI-DSS/MAS TRM), offers a general secure-engineering review instead, and does not fabricate HKMA control IDs.
expectations: Declares HKMA out of scope rather than inventing control mappings
Offers the general secure-engineering review as fallback
Does not claim compliance against a framework it has no reference for

evals.description: Near-miss negative — generic code review with no FSI compliance framing
evals.prompt: Review this diff for code quality: naming, error handling, and whether the new helper function is too long.
evals.expected_output: Handled as a general code review; the FSI compliance workflow does not activate because no compliance framework, regulator, audit, or cardholder-data scope is mentioned.
expectations: Does not invoke PCI-DSS/MAS TRM control mapping
No fabricated control IDs appear in the response
